title: Call composition and contract linter: SDK ergonomics + contract-testing PRD (ideation)
content:
Summary:
This is an ideation PRD for two interrelated deliveries: (1) a first-class SDK surface that makes composing multiple Hosted API interactions (generation, tool-calls, embeddings, reranking) ergonomic and testable; and (2) a developer-side contract linter + test harness that validates structured output and tool-call contracts against server-side schemas and example sessions. The goal is to reduce integration regressions, speed up developer iteration, and enable safe composition patterns for streaming and non-streaming flows.

Motivation / problem statements:
- Teams repeatedly implement fragile ad-hoc glue logic to stitch multiple API calls and tool invocations; bugs surface in production when response shapes or partial/streamed frames change.
- SDK ergonomics currently expose low-level stream frames and generic JSON blobs; engineers spend cycles writing brittle parsing/validation and end-to-end integration tests.
- Streaming + tool-call hybrid flows (partial responses that trigger tool calls, then resume streams) are particularly tricky to test locally and to assert correctness for.

Objectives (MVP):
1) SDK primitives for composable calls: a small set of higher-level APIs for composing call sequences, declaring intermediate contracts, and resuming streams after remote tool calls.
2) Contract Linter (local CLI): static checks against server-provided interface descriptors (schemas + permitted tool call signatures) that run on CI and locally.
3) Contract Test Harness: a lightweight harness that replays recorded server sessions (including partial frames) and validates SDK behavior end-to-end.
4) Developer docs and example apps for 3 common composition patterns: sequential tool pipeline, optimistic prefetch+tool, and resumable streaming tool-handshake.

Success metrics:
- 30% reduction in integration-related bug reports in the first 3 months after rollout (tracked via JIRA tags).
- >80% of new SDK integrations in internal test teams use the contract linter in CI within 6 weeks.
- Reduced mean time to fix contract regressions (time from incident to root cause) by 40% for tool-call related incidents.

User stories:
- As an app developer, I want a single composer function that takes a declarative sequence (generate -> parse -> call-tool -> generate) so I can reason about failure modes and retries without managing sockets manually.
- As an SDK author, I want a CLI linter that fails my CI when my expected output schema diverges from the model’s published schema so regressions are caught early.
- As an SRE/QA engineer, I want a harness that can replay intermittent partial frames to reproduce streaming resume issues deterministically.

Proposed API surface (sketch):
- ComposeSession({steps: [...], mode: "sync" | "stream", schemaMap: {...}}) -> session handle. Steps are typed descriptors: {type: "generate" | "call_tool" | "embed", name: "summarize", outputSchemaRef: "schemas/s1"} .
- session.on('delta', handler) and session.expect('schemaRef', assertionFn) helpers for tests.
- Client-side contract registration: hostClient.registerContract(id, {jsonSchema, version, exampleSessions}) - used by linter and harness.

Contract Linter (CLI) design notes:
- Invoked as: rw-contract-lint --contract contracts/order-extractor.json --examples examples/ --server-schema-url https://api.redwood.ai/contracts/latest
- Rules: schema compatibility (semver-like), forbidden-breaking-field-removals, allowed-added-optional-fields, enum-drift detection, tool-signature-compatibility.
- Integrations: GitHub Actions template, pre-commit hook for SDK projects.

Test Harness (replay):
- Stores compact session recordings: ordered frames with metadata (frame-type, timestamp, partial/prefix token count, tool-call markers).
- Harness playground can simulate slow networks, dropped frames, and resume from Nth frame to validate recovery logic.
- API: rw-contract-harness run --recordings examples/order-flow.rec --assertions tests/order-flow.assert.js

Streaming compatibility considerations:
- Need deterministic mapping between recorded partial frames and SDK resume points. Recording should capture both token deltas and KW (keyed) frame boundaries used by server.
- Composer API must expose a clear transactional boundary when a tool call is issued mid-stream (flush semantics, client-side buffering window, timeout semantics).

Backward/forward compatibility strategy:
- Server will publish contract manifests with version tags and a compatibility matrix. Linter will flag major-version mismatches.
- Provide opt-in runtime strictness flags: strict (throw on mismatch), warn (log only), permissive (best-effort). CI default recommended: strict for production packages, warn for experimental.

Developer experience (DX) flows:
- Rapid iteration: developer scaffolds compose-session from VSCode snippet; linter runs on save in CI; harness replays failing sessions locally with an interactive UI that shows frame-by-frame differences.
- Debugging: SDK exposes a --trace-frames option which serializes frames in NDJSON for easy diffing and minimal PII by default.

Rollout plan (phases):
- Phase 0 (3 weeks): prototype composer API + simple inline linter using local server schemas; internal dogfooding with 2 product teams.
- Phase 1 (6 weeks): CLI linter + GitHub Action; test harness MVP with recording/replay; docs and 3 example apps.
- Phase 2 (6 weeks): polish, performance hardening of composer (latency for streaming paths), integrate with console observability and telemetry to surface linter/contract alerts.

Open questions / risks:
- How large are the server-provided schemas and how frequently will they change? Frequent churn increases noise. Plan: server to publish change logs and deprecation windows.
- Recording sensitivity: session recordings may include user content; need redaction/PII rules by default.
- Runtime cost: composer buffering and replayed tests may add memory/CPU; need caps for mobile SDK variants.

Dependencies:
- Server: contract manifest endpoint + versioned schema store (API work).
- Infra: storage for recorded sessions (S3 + retention policy) and UI for interactive replay (Console).
- SDK: language bindings (JS, Python) and pre-commit hook distribution.

Next steps for MVP:
1) Prod team sync to validate 3 canonical composition patterns and pick sample apps for dogfooding. (Owner: Asha)
2) Engineering spike: implement minimal ComposeSession JS prototype that can: orchestrate generate -> call_tool -> resume stream. (Owner: Elliot)
3) Fast-fail linter PoC that validates a small schema set with GitHub Action integration. (Owner: Marisol)
4) Safety/PII review for recording format and default redaction. (Owner: Diego)

Appendix: example developer vignette (short)
- John builds a shipping assistant: he writes a contract 'order-extractor' JSON schema, uses ComposeSession to declare generation -> parse -> call_payment -> confirm -> summarize. He runs rw-contract-lint in CI and the action fails when the model returns a subtle enum change. He re-runs the harness locally to replay the session, narrows the issue to a server change, and updates the contract with a migration. Total iteration time: 2 hours vs previous ~2 days.

This doc is intentionally ideation-level; feedback welcome on API ergonomics, policy for recording retention/redaction, and recommended CI defaults.
